fields.logicalExtension.pro.newArguments.0.text: A defensible accommodation should contain an internal mechanism that reduces dependence on the tolerated wrong. The defense could argue that release provisions, fugitive refuge, redemption rights, manumission practices, and shared worship form such a mechanism when read cumulatively. This would improve the trajectory case by specifying measurable institutional pressure toward freedom, while conceding that any passage lacking an exit mechanism remains especially difficult for the account.
fields.logicalExtension.pro.newArguments.1.text: The defense can distinguish surface legal permission from a canon’s governing moral norms by testing interpretations for coherence with creation, liberation, neighbor-love, and equal standing before God. If those themes possess interpretive priority, permissions should be read narrowly as emergency governance rather than timeless authorization. The argument succeeds only if that priority is independently justified and consistently applied to permanent foreign slavery, not merely asserted when a text becomes morally embarrassing.

finalArgument.thesis: Biblical slavery regulations are morally defensible only when interpreted as constrained accommodations ordered toward universal human freedom and equal dignity.
premises: A morally perfect lawgiver may temporarily regulate entrenched wrongdoing when immediate prohibition would predictably produce greater violence, abandonment, or social collapse.
Biblical laws restrict kidnapping, recognize refuge for fugitives, limit some service, and repeatedly remind Israel of its own liberation from bondage.
The wider canon grounds every person’s worth in divine creation, commands neighbor-love, and portrays redemption as liberation rather than domination.
Later Christian equality language destabilizes status hierarchy by treating enslaved and free believers as siblings with the same standing before God.
A coherent canonical reading interprets particular permissions through these controlling moral commitments while refusing to redescribe coercive ownership as intrinsically good.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore the regulations can be defended as harm-limiting concessions within a reforming moral trajectory, although coercive ownership itself remains contrary to the canon’s governing ideals.

newArguments.title: Accommodation Requires Exit
newArguments.text: A defensible accommodation should contain an internal mechanism that reduces dependence on the tolerated wrong. The defense could argue that release provisions, fugitive refuge, redemption rights, manumission practices, and shared worship form such a mechanism when read cumulatively. This would improve the trajectory case by specifying measurable institutional pressure toward freedom, while conceding that any passage lacking an exit mechanism remains especially difficult for the account.

newArguments.title: Authority Under Moral Unity
newArguments.text: The defense can distinguish surface legal permission from a canon’s governing moral norms by testing interpretations for coherence with creation, liberation, neighbor-love, and equal standing before God. If those themes possess interpretive priority, permissions should be read narrowly as emergency governance rather than timeless authorization. The argument succeeds only if that priority is independently justified and consistently applied to permanent foreign slavery, not merely asserted when a text becomes morally embarrassing.
